tool.name: FoldMason
tool.description: align protein structures or sequences using structural information
tool.command: #import re #if str($source.mode) == 'structures' #set $structures = $source.structures @LINK_STRUCTURES@ #else #set $sequence_ext = 'fasta.gz' if $source.sequences.is_of_type('fasta.gz') else 'fasta' ln -s '$source.sequences' 'sequences.$sequence_ext' && #end if foldmason easy-msa #if str($source.mode) == 'structures' structures/* result tmp --report-mode $source.report_mode #else 'sequences.$sequence_ext' result tmp --prostt5-model '$source.model.fields.path' --report-mode 0 --gpu 0 #end if --threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" $alignment.fast $alignment.precluster --refine-iters $alignment.refine_iters --refine-seed $alignment.refine_seed --pair-threshold $alignment.pair_threshold #if $alignment.guide_tree --guide-tree '$alignment.guide_tree' #end if > '$log'

param.label: Structural alignment report
param.option: Interactive HTML report with LDDT scores

param.name: sequences
param.label: Protein sequences
param.help: Provide at least two amino acid sequences. ProstT5 predicts 3Di structural tokens, rather than atomic coordinates.

param.name: model
param.label: ProstT5 model
param.help: Select Foldseek-compatible GGUF weights installed by your Galaxy administrator. Requires a FoldMason package built with ProstT5 support.

tool.help:
**What it does**
FoldMason builds multiple protein alignments using amino acid sequences and the 3Di structural alphabet. Supply PDB/mmCIF structures, or protein sequences to predict 3Di tokens with ProstT5 on the CPU.
**Inputs**
For structures, select at least two datasets or a collection. Dataset names become alignment identifiers after removing PDB/mmCIF extensions and replacing special characters with underscores; use unique names. Each structure chain may produce a separate sequence.
For sequence input, supply a protein FASTA containing at least two sequences and select an installed ProstT5 model. This requires a FoldMason build with ProstT5 enabled and compatible ``prostt5-f16.gguf`` weights. Your administrator registers these in the shared Hugging Face data table. The original Hugging Face Transformers weights cannot be used directly.
**Outputs**
The tool returns amino acid and 3Di alignments in FASTA format, a Newick guide tree, and a log. Structure inputs can additionally produce an interactive HTML or JSON report with LDDT scores. Sequence inputs lack atomic coordinates, so FoldMason uses fast alignment and cannot produce coordinate-based LDDT reports.
**Options**
Fast mode disables neighbourhood scoring. Preclustering can speed up large alignments. Refinement iterations improve the initial alignment; the random seed makes repeated refinement runs reproducible. An optional guide tree must use the same identifiers as the inputs.
